drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 85-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.68, creatinine 2.16-2.21, hemoglobin 13.3-13.5, platelets 303-304, sodium 139, wbc 6.6; vitals dbp 73-78, heart_rate 75-79, map 92-95, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 13-15, sbp 127-129, spo2 96-98, temp 37-37.2
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Chronic kidney disease stage 3. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient seen and examined at bedside. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 2.21-2.22, hemoglobin 13.5, platelets 307-308, sodium 139, wbc 5.9-6.5; vitals dbp 75-78, heart_rate 78-81, map 94-96, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 13-15, sbp 131-133, spo2 97-98, temp 37-37.2
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Chronic kidney disease stage 3. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 85-year-old male, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Chronic kidney disease stage 3. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
